The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief says?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do not blame him, for he is a man of great jealousy (ghayrah). By Allah, he has never married a woman except a virgin, and he has never divorced a woman, so a man among us has dared to marry her out of the intensity of his jealousy.' Sa'd said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I know that it is the truth and that it is from Allah, the Exalted, but I was amazed that if I found a lakā' (a loose woman) with a man between her thighs, I would not be permitted to stir him or move him until I brought four witnesses. By Allah, I will not bring them until he has finished his need.' He said: 'They did not wait long before Hilal ibn Umayyah, who was one of the three whose repentance was accepted, came in the morning to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger, I came to my family at night and found with her a man. I saw with my own eyes and heard with my own ears."'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked what he had brought and was distressed by it. The Ansar gathered and said: 'We have been afflicted with what Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said. Now the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) will strike Hilal ibn Umayyah and his testimony among the Muslims will be nullified.' Hilal said: 'By Allah, I hope that Allah, the Exalted, will make a way out for me from it.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I see what has distressed you about what I have brought, and Allah, the Exalted, knows that I am truthful.' By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was about to order that he be struck when revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). When revelation descended upon him (peace be upon him), they recognised it by the change in the color of his skin. They refrained from him until he finished with the revelation, and then the verse was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ — the verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved and said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for I was hoping for this from my Lord." He (peace be upon him) also said: "Send for her." She came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to them both, admonished them, and informed them that the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe than the punishment of this world.' Hilal said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, she has indeed spoken the truth about me.' She said: 'He lied.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Separate them (ʿannū baynahumā).'" The hadith [continues]. Included in it, and likewise in another narration mentioned by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, and al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, is that the story of Hilal is the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of the verse.

It was said that it was revealed concerning 'Asim ibn 'Adi, and it was said concerning 'Uwaymir ibn Nasr al-'Ajlani. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari there is something that supports this. Indeed, al-Suhayli said that this is the correct view, and that the other was attributed to error. The well-known view, as in al-Bahr (al-Bahr al-Muhit), is that the incident of Hilal came before the incident of 'Uwaymir.

Abu Ya'la and Ibn Mardawayh related from Anas that he said: "The first li'an (mutual oath of condemnation) in Islam was what occurred between Hilal ibn Umayyah and his wife."

Al-Khafaji here quoted from al-Subki a difficulty, and he said: "It is a difficult problem that applies to the verses of li'an, theft and fornication, namely that what contains a conditional (shart) is explicit in causation (ʿillah) together with the fa' (the particle of consequence), and it may also bear that meaning without it. Since it is treated as a conditional, the action it contains is future, not past, so its ruling does not extend back to what preceded it, and it does not include the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul), which is past."

He (al-Subki) was answered: there is no difficulty in this at all; rather it is easier than drinking cold water in the heat of summer, because this and similar expressions mean: "If you wish to know this ruling, it is such-and-such." So the future refers to knowing its ruling and implementing it, and this is future both in the occasion of revelation and in other cases. The indication that the intended meaning is this is that it was revealed concerning a past matter, and its ruling was intended to be made clear. For this reason they said: "The inclusion of the occasion of revelation is definite."

There is no need to say that the conditional may enter upon the past, nor that what contains a conditional does not necessarily equal its explicit form in every respect, nor that the inclusion of what was mentioned is by way of indication (dalalat al-nass) — since that is invalid here. End of quotation.

Then, the meaning here is similar to what has passed: ﴿those who accuse their wives of fornication﴾, whether they have consummated the marriage with them or not, and likewise the women undergoing the waiting period (ʿiddah) after a revocable divorce. ﴿And they have no witnesses﴾, four persons who testify to what they accused them of, namely fornication. It is read takun (with the feminine ta above) — and the reading of the majority is more eloquent. ﴿Except themselves﴾ is a substitute (badal) for (shuhada') because the statement is not affirmative (ghayr mujab), and the preferred choice in it is substitution. Or illa is in the meaning of ghayr (other than), an adjective (sifah) for shuhada', and its i'rab (grammatical inflection) appears on what follows it because it is in the form of a particle, just as they said regarding the al- that is the relative pronoun entering upon the active participles, for example.

Including them among the witnesses, as it has been said, is a notification from the very beginning that their statement is not to be entirely disregarded, and that it is placed within the category of testimony. With this, the beauty of attributing testimony to them increases, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So the testimony of one of them﴾, i.e., the testimony of each one of them. It is the subject (mubtada') and His saying, glorified is He: ﴿four testimonies﴾ is its predicate (khabar), i.e., their prescribed testimony is four testimonies. ﴿By Allah﴾ is related to "testimonies" (shahadat), and some scholars allowed that it is related to "testimony" (shahadah).

It is objected to this that it then necessitates separating the verbal noun from its complement by a foreign element, namely the predicate. You know that the predicate being a foreign element is a matter of discussion, and that some grammarians permitted the separation absolutely, and some permitted it when the complement is an adverbial (zarf), as it is here.

Most read ﴿arba'a﴾ (four) in the accusative, as a verbal noun (masdar), and the governing element in it is "testimony" (shahadah), which is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "so what is required is testimony," or it is the subject whose predicate is omitted, i.e., "so upon them is testimony," or "so the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah, obligatory or sufficient." There is no disagreement about the permissibility of the prepositional phrase being related, in this reading, to either the testimony or the testimonies, and the disagreement is only about the first.

﴿Indeed he is among the truthful﴾, i.e., in what he accused her of, namely fornication. The original is "that he is," etc., so the preposition was deleted, inna was made with a kasrah, and the governing verb was suspended from it by the lam of emphasis. Suspension is not restricted to verbs of the heart, but occurs also in what goes in their direction, and among them is "testimony," because it conveys knowledge. It was also permitted that the sentence be the response to an oath, based on the view that testimony here means oath. So al-Raghib said: "It is understood from it that, even if 'by Allah' is not mentioned." The verification of this will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.

"And the fifth" — that is, the fifth testimony, which completes the four preceding ones, making them five by being added to them. Its being singled out, though it too is a testimony, is because it stands on its own in meaning (bi-l-fahwa) and is emphatic (wakadatuha) in conveying what the one giving testimony intends: establishing the report as true and manifesting truthfulness. It is a subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is the statement of the Exalted: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars﴾ regarding what he accused her of, namely adultery.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 24, verse 8:

﴿Wa-yadra'u﴾ means yadfa'u (he averts), ﴿'anha al-'adhab﴾: i.e., the worldly punishment, which is imprisonment according to us (the Hanafis) and the hadd (prescribed legal punishment) according to al-Shafi'i. Its detailed discussion will come, God willing, ﴿that she bear witness four times by God that he﴾, i.e., the husband,
Page 106
﴿is surely among the liars﴾ concerning what he accused her of, namely adultery.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 24, verse 9 (part 1 of 3):

﴿And the fifth﴾ is in the accusative, coordinated with ﴿four testimonies﴾. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that the wrath of God be upon her if he [i.e., the husband] is among the truthful﴾ concerning what he accused her of, of adultery, is with the preposition elided, meaning "that the wrath of God…" and so on. It is also permitted for ﴿that﴾ and what follows it to be in apposition to ﴿the fifth﴾. The specification of wrath to the woman's side is for emphasis against her, because she is the source of immorality, and because women often use cursing frequently, so they may be bold in uttering it, since its weight has fallen from their hearts, unlike His wrath, majestic is His majesty.

Talha, al-Hasan, al-A'mash and Khalid ibn Iyas read ﴿al-khamisatu﴾ with the accusative in both places. You have already learned the reason for the accusative in the second place. As for the reason for the accusative in the first, it is the coordination of ﴿al-khamisata﴾ with ﴿arba'a shahadatin﴾ according to the reading of whoever put ﴿arba'a﴾ in the accusative, and made it the object of an elided verb indicated by the meaning according to the reading of whoever put ﴿arba'a﴾ in the nominative, meaning "and he testifies the fifth." The discussion of ﴿that the curse of God…﴾ and so on is as you have heard in ﴿that the wrath…﴾ and so on.

Nafi' read ﴿anna la'nata﴾ with the light ﴿anna﴾ and the nominative ﴿la'nata﴾, and ﴿anna ghadaba﴾ with the light ﴿an﴾, with ﴿ghadaba﴾ a past verb and the divine name following it in the nominative. In both places ﴿an﴾ is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter. Neither of the separators was placed between ﴿qad﴾ and the ﴿sin﴾, nor between it and the verb in the second place, because the verb carries the sense of supplication. So there is in that the parallel of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that blessed is whoever is in the fire﴾ [An-Naml: 8]. Thus there is no strangeness in this reading, contrary to what the words of Ibn 'Atiyya seem to imply.

al-Hasan, Abu Raja', Qatada, 'Isa, Salam, 'Amr ibn Maymun, al-A'raj and Ya'qub, with a variant from them both, read ﴿an la'nata﴾ like Nafi's reading, and ﴿anna ghadaba﴾ with the light ﴿an﴾ and ﴿ghadaba﴾ as a nominative verbal noun. This is the apparent sense of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾, in its generality. What is mentioned in the books of our companions is that the accuser and the wife he has accused must both be qualified to give testimony against a Muslim. Therefore li'an (mutual imprecation) does not take place between disbelievers or slaves, nor when either of them is a slave, a minor, insane, or one who has been subjected to the hadd (prescribed punishment) for qadhf (slander). It is also required of the wife that she be chaste from adultery, and that she not be suspected of it, meaning that she has not been intimate with a person forbidden to her by essence, even once, by mistaken right or by an invalid marriage, and that she has no child without a known father in the city where the slander occurred. The requirement of this is because li'an stands in place of the hadd for slander with respect to the husband, as the report we have previously mentioned indicates. However, this applies to each wife individually, not generally. Do you not see that if he slanders four words or four women to whom he is married with adultery, one li'an for them does not suffice him, but he must impose li'an on each of them? And if he slanders four strangers in this way, he incurs one hadd for all of them. So whenever the wife is not one whose slanderer incurs the hadd, as when she is not chaste, the slander against her does not meet what requires the hadd, so that li'an would take its place. As for the requirement that they both be qualified to give testimony, it is because li'an is testimonies reinforced by oaths according to us, unlike al-Shafi'i, who holds that it is reinforced oaths. This is the apparent view of the words of Malik and Ahmad. So it occurs from one who is qualified to swear, and that is one who has the power of divorce. Thus, according to him, whoever has that power is qualified for li'an, so it occurs from every sane husband, even if he is a disbeliever or a slave.

He cited as evidence that li'an is reinforced oaths His saying, glorified is He, ﴿then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by God﴾. That is because His saying, ﴿by God﴾, is decisive in the sense of oath, while testimony is open to the sense of oath. Do you not see that if he says "I testify" and intends by it an oath, it is an oath? So the ambiguous is interpreted in light of the decisive, because taking it in its literal sense is impossible, since what is known in the sacred law is that a person's testimony for himself is not accepted, unlike his oath. Likewise, what is known in the sacred law is that testimony is not repeated in one setting, unlike oaths, for their repetition is known in the qasama (oath procedure in homicide cases). Also, testimony's domain is establishment, while oath is for negation, so it is not conceivable that the literal senses of both attach to one matter. Therefore it is necessary to act on the literal meaning of one of them and the figurative meaning of the other, so let the figurative be the word "testimony," because of the two premises you have heard.

Our companions cited as evidence that they are testimonies reinforced by oaths the same verse, because taking the literal meaning is required when possible. His saying, glorified and exalted is He, ﴿And they had no witnesses except themselves﴾ affirms that they are witnesses, because an exception from a negation is an affirmation. If "witnesses" is taken figuratively as "swearers," the meaning becomes "they had no swearers except themselves," which is not sound, because it implies that if those who accuse their wives have no one to swear for them, they swear for themselves. This is a branch that presupposes a person swearing on behalf of another, and no such thing exists at all. So if the meaning of oath were the literal meaning of the word "testimony," this would be a barrier turning it to its figurative sense. How much more so, since it is figurative for it. And if this were not the case, the possibility of acting on the literal meaning would necessitate not interpreting it as oath. How much more so, since this is a barrier against the figurative. What was supposed to be a barrier, from what has been mentioned, is not necessary. Your saying, "acceptance of testimony for oneself and repetition of the testimony" are not established, we say: both swearing on behalf of another and swearing to establish a ruling are not established. Rather, oath is for lifting a ruling. If it is permissible for the sacred law to prescribe these two matters in one specific context initially, it is also permissible for that to be prescribed initially. Indeed, it is closer, because of the rationality that multiplying it to four in place of what he is unable to do, namely bringing witnesses to adultery, who are four, and the non-acceptance of testimony from him when there is suspicion. For this reason it is firmly established when they are absent, as God, mighty and majestic is He, said: ﴿God bears witness that there is no god but He﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 18]. So it is not far-fetched that it is prescribed when its strength is weakened, through reinforcing it with an oath and imposing the curse and wrath if he is lying, while the consequence of each testimony does not apply to each of the two witnesses. For the consequence of the testimony of each is a hadd upon the other, and that is not established here. Rather, what is established by the two testimonies is what is established by the oaths, which is the cancellation of each one's claim against the other. It is said "by both of them" rather than "from both of them," because this cancellation is not the consequence of the two testimonies, but the consequence of their conflict. As for his saying, "and the oath is for negation," etc., its place is where it is made in denial of a claimant's claim. Otherwise, it may be sworn about an informative matter of negation or affirmation, and here it is like that, for it is on his truthfulness in the testimony. The truth is that it is on what the testimony was about, which is that he is among the truthful in what he accused her of, just as when one gathers oaths on one matter he reports. This is the real sense of their being reinforcement of the testimony, for if their objects differed, neither would reinforce the other.

An objection was raised against the requirement of qualification for giving testimony: they said that li'an takes place between the blind and the wicked, although neither of them is qualified for it. The answer given is that they are qualified for giving testimony, but it is not accepted from the wicked, and the blind cannot distinguish between the one testified for and the one testified against. Here, however, he is able to separate himself from his wife, so he is qualified for this testimony and not for other testimonies. Ibn al-Mubarak reported from Abu Hanifa that the blind man does not perform li'an. Al-Qahastani generalized the qualification, saying: "Even by the judgment of the judge, and the wicked person's testimony is valid for judgment, and likewise the blind person's testimony is valid on the view of its validity in matters established by hearsay, such as death, marriage, and lineage. This is unlike one who has been subjected to the hadd for qadhf, whose testimony is not valid for judgment." Perhaps what Ibn Kamal Pasha meant by his saying, "if he judges by the testimony of one who has been subjected to the hadd for qadhf, it is effective, like the effectiveness of the ruling based on its validity by someone who holds it valid, like a Shafi'i, according to what is said," is contrary to the apparent sense of his words, as is not hidden from one who refers to it.

It is required that the qadhf be within the Abode of Islam, and that it be by explicit mention of adultery. There is no li'an for qadhf by sodomy according to Abu Hanifa, while according to the two companions there is li'an for it. Nor is there li'an for qadhf by allusion or indirect implication. Qadhf by its explicit wording is such as saying: "You are an adulteress," or "O adulteress," or "I saw you committing adultery." According to the well-known view of Malik, qadhf with the first two wordings necessitates the hadd, while what necessitates li'an is qadhf with the last, and this is the view of al-Layth, Uthman, and Yahya ibn Sa'id. This was deemed weak, because all were accused of adultery, and that is the cause, as the verse indicates, so there is no difference. Equivalent to explicit qadhf is denying the paternity of her child, whether from him or from another.

In al-Muhit and al-Mubtaghi: if the husband denies the child, saying, "This is not my son," without accusing her of adultery, there is no li'an between them, because denial is not an explicit accusation of her with adultery, since it is certain that the child may be from another through a mistaken intercourse. This is a fallen possibility that is not to be considered, as Zayn (Ibn Nujaym) verified in al-Bahr. It is required for li'an to be obligatory that the wife request it in the presence of the judge, as in al-Bada'i', if the qadhf is by explicit adultery, because li'an is her right, since it is for removing shame from her. The three imams also said so. If the qadhf is by denial of the child, then the accuser's request is required, because it is also his right, since he needs to deny someone who is not his child from himself. This denial is obligatory for him if he is certain the child is not his, because silence or acknowledgment would be an affiliation of one who is not his, and that is forbidden, like denying the lineage of one who is his. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when the verse of li'an was revealed: "Any woman who introduces into a people one who is not of them, she has nothing to do with God, and God will not admit her into His Paradise. And any man who denies his child while he is looking at him, God, mighty and majestic is He, will veil Himself from him on the Day of Resurrection, and will expose him before the first and the last." If it is possible the child is his, then he should not deny it, though it may be permitted, and it may be contrary to what is better, according to the strength or weakness of the possibility. The possibility may weaken to a degree where denial is not permitted, such as when his wife, known for chastity, bears a child that does not resemble him.

Concerning Abu Hurayra: a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "My wife has given birth to a black boy." He said: "Do you have camels?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What are their colors?" He said: "Red." He said: "Is there among them a grayish one?" He said: "Yes." He said: "How is that?" He said: "A vein pulled it." He said: "Perhaps this one was pulled by a vein."

They mentioned regarding the case where she is suspected of having a man, and then bears a child resembling him, two views: that denial is permitted, and that it is not. As for explicit qadhf with adultery, when it is certain, it is permitted, and it is allowed to conceal it for her and keep her, based on the apparent meaning of what was reported: that a man said: "O Messenger of God, my wife does not turn away the hand of a touching man." He said: "Divorce her." He said: "I love her." He said: "Then keep her."

وفيه احتمال آخر ذكره شراح الحديث، لكن مع عدم التحقق لا يباح ذلك. والأفضل للزوجة ألا تطالب باللعان (mutual imprecation, *li'an*) وأن تستر الأمر، وللحاكم أن يأمرها بذلك. وإذا طلبت، وقد أقر الزوج بقذفها، أو ثبت ذلك بالبينة وكانت البينة رجلين لا رجلا وامرأتين، لأنه لا شهادة للنساء في الحدود، فإن ما في *النهر* و*الدر المنتقى* من جواز ذلك قد سبق قلم لاعن، إن كان مصرا وعجز عن البينة على زناها، أو على إقرارها به، أو على تصديقها له، أو أقام البينة على ذلك ثم عمي الشاهدان أو فسقا أو ارتدا. وهذا بخلاف ما إذا ماتا أو غابا بعد أن عدلا، فإنه حينئذ لا يقضى باللعان. فإن امتنع، حد حد القذف (*hadd al-qadhf*، the prescribed punishment for slander). وكذلك إذا لاعن فامتنعت، فعنده (أي عند الشافعي) تحد حد الزنا، وعندنا تحبس حتى تلاعن أو تصدقه، فيرتفع سبب وجوب لعانهما، وهو التكاذب على ما قيل. والأوجه أن السبب هو القذف، والتكاذب شرطه. وكما لا لعان مع التصديق إذا كان بلفظ «صدقت»، فلا حد عليها، ولو أعادت ذلك أربع مرات في مجالس متفرقة، لأن التصديق المذكور ليس بإقرار قصدا وبالذات، فلا يعتبر في وجوب الحد بل في درئه، فينتفي به اللعان ولا يوجب به الحد. وكذلك ينتفي بذلك الحد عن قاذفها بعد، كما في *كافي الحاكم*. ولو صدقته في نفي الولد فلا حد ولا لعان أيضا، وهو ولدهما، لأن النسب إنما ينقطع بحكم اللعان ولم يوجد، وهو حق الولد، فلا يصدقان في إبطاله. وما في *شرحي الوقاية* و*النقاية* من أنها إذا صدقته ينتفي الولد غير صحيح، كما نبه عليه في *شرح الدرر والغرر*.

ووجه قول الشافعي بالحد عند الامتناع أن الواجب بالقذف مطلقا هو الحد، لعموم قوله سبحانه: ﴿والذين يرمون المحصنات﴾ إلخ (*And those who accuse chaste women*…)، إلا أنه يتمكن من دفعه فيما إذا كانت المقذوفة زوجة باللعان تخفيفا عليه، فإذا لم يدفعه به حد. وكذلك المرأة تلاعن بعد ما أوجب الزوج عليها اللعان بلعانه، فإذا امتنعت حدت للزنا. ويشير إليه قوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ويدرأ عنها العذاب﴾ (*and it averts the punishment from her*). ووجه قولنا إن قوله تعالى: ﴿والذين يرمون أزواجهم﴾ إلى قوله تعالى: ﴿فشهادة أحدهم﴾ إلخ (*And those who accuse their wives… then the testimony of one of them*…) يفهم منه، كيفما كانت القراءة، أن الواجب في قذف الزوجات هو اللعان، ولا ينكر ذلك إلا مكابر. فإما أن يكون ناسخا أو مخصصا لعموم ذلك العام، والظاهر عندنا أنه ناسخ لتراخي نزوله، كما تشهد له الأخبار الصحيحة، والمخصص لا يكون متراخي النزول. وعلى التقديرين يلزم أن يكون الحكم الثابت في قذف الزوجات إنما هو ما تضمنته الآية من اللعان حال قيام الزوجية، كما هو الظاهر، فلا يجب غيره عند الامتناع عن إيفائه، بل يحبس لإيفائه، كما في كل حق امتنع من هو عليه عن إيفائه. ولم يتعين كون المراد من العذاب في الآية الحد، لجواز كونه الحبس. وإذا قام الدليل على أن اللعان هو الواجب، وجب حمله عليه.

قيل: والعجب من الشافعي عليه الرحمة (*may Allah have mercy on him*) أنه لا يقبل شهادة الزوج عليها بالزنا مع ثلاثة عدول، ثم يوجب الحد عليها بقوله وحده وإن كان عبدا فاسقا. وأعجب منه أن اللعان يمين عنده، وهو لا يصلح لإيجاب المال ولا لإسقاطه بعد الوجوب، وقد أسقط به كل من الرجل والمرأة الحد عن نفسه، وأوجب به الرجم الذي هو أغلظ الحدود على المرأة. فإن قال: إنما يوجبه عليها لنكولها بامتناعها عن اللعان، قلنا: هو أيضا من ذلك العجب، فإن كون النكول إقرارا فيه شبهة، والحد مما يندفع بها، مع أنه غاية ما يكون بمنزلة إقراره مرة. ثم إن هذه الشبهة أثرت عنده في منع إيجاب المال، مع أنه يثبت مع الشبهة، فكيف يوجب الرجم به وهو أغلظ الحدود وأصعبها إثباتا وأكثرها شروطا؟ انتهى. وليراجع في ذلك كتب الشافعية. وفي *النهر* نقلا عن *الأسبيجابي* أنهما يحبسان إذا امتنعا عن اللعان بعد الثبوت، ثم قال: وينبغي حمله على ما إذا لم تعف المرأة، كما في *البحر*. وعندي في حبسها بعد امتناعه نوع إشكال، لأن اللعان لا يجب عليها إلا بعد لعانه، فقبله ليس امتناعا لحق وجب عليها. انتهى.

وأجاب الطحاوي (*al-Tahawi*) بأنه بعد الترافع منهما صار إمضاء اللعان حق الشرع، فإذا لم تعف وأظهرت الامتناع تحبس، بخلاف ما إذا أبى هو فقط فلا تحبس. انتهى.

وقيل: ليس المراد امتناعهما في آن واحد، بل المراد امتناعه بعد المطالبة به، وامتناعها بعد لعانه، فتأمل.

والمتبادر من الشهادة ما كان قولا حقيقة، ولذا قالوا: لا لعان لو كانا أخرسين أو أحدهما، لفقد الركن، وهو لفظ «أشهد». وعلل أيضا بأن هناك شبهة احتمال تصديق أحدهما للآخر لو كان ناطقا، والحد يدرأ بالشبهة. وكتابة الأخرس في هذا الفصل كإشارته لا يعول عليها. وذكروا لو طرأ الخرس بعد اللعان قبل التفريق، فلا تفريق ولا حد. ويشعر ظاهر الآية بتقديم لعان الزوج، وهو المأثور في السنة، فلو بدأ القاضي بأمرها فلاعنت قبله فقد أخطأ السنة، ولا يجب، كما في *الغاية*، أن تعيد لعانها بعد، وبه قال مالك.

وفي *البدائع*: ينبغي أن تعيد، لأن اللعان شهادة المرأة، وشهادتها تقدح في شهادة الزوج، فلا تصح إلا بعد وجود شهادته، ولهذا يبدأ بشهادة المدعي في باب الدعوى، ثم بشهادة المدعى عليه بطريق الدفع له. ونقل ذلك عن الشافعي وأحمد عليهما الرحمة، وأشهب من المالكية. والوجه ما تقدم، فقد أعقب في الآية الرمي بشهادة أحدهم وشهادتها الدارئة عنها العذاب، فيكون هذا المجموع بعد الرمي، وليس في الآية ما يدل على الترتيب بين أجزاء المجموع. وهذا نظير ما قرره بعض (أجلة) الأصحاب في قوله تعالى: ﴿إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيديكم إلى المرافق﴾ [المائدة: 6] الآية، في بيان أنه لا يدل على فرضية الترتيب كما يقوله الشافعية. وظاهر الآية أنه لا يجب في لعانه أن يأتي بضمير المخاطبة، ولا في لعانها أن تأتي بضمير المخاطب. فقد جاء في *الهداية* صفة اللعان أن

[p. 110]

يبتدئ به القاضي، فيشهد أربع مرات، يقول في كل مرة: أشهد بالله إني لمن الصادقين فيما رميتها به من الزنا، ويقول في الخامسة: لعنة الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين فيما رميتها به من الزنا، يشير في جميع ذلك. ثم تشهد المرأة أربع مرات، تقول في كل مرة: أشهد بالله إنه لمن الكاذبين فيما رماني به من الزنا، وتقول في الخامسة: غضب الله عليها إن كان من الصادقين فيما رماني به من الزنا. والأصل فيه الآية. ورَوى الحسن عن أبي حنيفة أنه يأتي بلفظة المواجهة ويقول: فيما رميتك به من الزنا، أي وتأتي هي بذلك أيضا وتقول: إنك لمن الكاذبين فيما رميتني به من الزنا، لأنه أقطع للاحتمال، وهو احتمال إضمار مرجع للضمير الغائب غير المراد. ووجه الأول أن لفظة المغايبة إذا انضمت إليها الإشارة انقطع الاحتمال. وعن الليث أنه يكتفى في اللعان بالكيفية المذكورة في الآية، ويأتي الملاعن مكان ضمير الغائب بضمير المتكلم في شهادته مطلقا، وتأتي الملاعنة بذلك في شهادتها الخامسة فتدخل على (على) ياء الضمير. والمراد من الاكتفاء بالكيفية المذكورة أنه لا يحتاج إلى زيادة فيما رميتها به من الزنا في شهادته، وإلى زيادة فيما رماني به من الزنا في شهادتها. وما ذكر من الإتيان بضمير المتكلم هو الظاهر، ولم يؤت به في النظم الكريم لتتسق الضمائر وتكون في جميع الآية على طراز واحد، مع ما في ذلك من نكتة رعاية التالي على ما قيل. وليس في الآية التفات أصلا كما توهم بعض من أدركناه من فضلاء العصر. وأما ما أشير من عدم الاحتياج إلى زيادة ما تقدم، فالظاهر أن الأحوط خلافه، وقد جاءت تلك الزيادة فيما وقع في زمانه ﷺ من اللعان بين هلال وزوجته على ما في بعض الروايات. وذكر الأصحاب أنه يزيد في صورة اللعان بالقذف بنفي الولد بعد قوله: لمن الصادقين، قوله: فيما رميتك به من نفي الولد، وأنها تزيد بعد لمن الكاذبين قولها: فيما رميتني به من نفي الولد. ولو كان القذف بالزنا ونفي الولد ذكر في اللعان الأمران. ونقل أبو حيان عن مالك أن الملاعن يقول: أشهد بالله إني رأيتها تزني، والملاعنة تقول: أشهد بالله ما رآني أزني. وعن الشافعي أن الزوج يقول: أشهد بالله إني لصادق فيما رميت به زوجتي فلانة بنت فلان، ويشير إليها إن كانت حاضرة، أربع مرات، ثم يقعده الإمام ويذكره الله تعالى، فإن رآه يريد أن يمضي أمر من يضع يده على فيه، فإن لم يمتنع تركه، وحينئذ يقول الخامسة ويأتي بياء الضمير مع (على). وإن كان قد قذفها بأحد يسميه بعينه واحدا أو اثنين في كل شهادة، وإن نفى ولدها زاد: وإن هذا الولد ولد زنا ما هو مني. والتخويف بالله عز وجل مشروع في حق المتلاعنين، فقد صح في قصة هلال أنه لما كان الخامسة قيل له: اتق الله تعالى واحذر عقابه، فإن عذاب الدنيا أسهل من عذاب الآخرة، وإن هذه هي الموجبة التي توجب عليك العقاب. وقيل: نحو ذلك لامرأته عند الخامسة أيضا.

وفي ظاهر الآية رد على الشافعي عليه الرحمة (*may Allah have mercy on him*) حيث قال إنه بمجرد لعان الزوج تثبت الفرقة بينهما. وذلك لأن المتبادر أنها تشهد الشهادات وهي زوجة، ومتى كانت الفرقة بلعان الزوج لم تبق زوجة عند لعانها. والذي ذهب إليه أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة أنه إذا وقع التلاعن تثبت حرمة الوطء ودواعيه عن الملاعن، فإن طلقها فذاك، وإن لم يطلقها بانت بتفريق الحاكم وإن لم يرضيا بالفرقة. ولو فرق خطأ بعد وجود الأكثر من كل منهما صح. ويشترط كون التفريق بحضورهما وحضور الوكيل كحضور الأصيل، ويتوارثان قبله. ولو زالت أهلية اللعان بعده، فإن كان بما يرجى زواله كجنون فرق، وإلا لا. وقال زفر: تقع الفرقة بتلاعنهما، وإن أكذب نفسه من بعد اللعان والتفريق وحُدّ أم لم يحد، يحل له تزوجها عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد. وقال أبو يوسف: إذا افترق المتلاعنان

[p. 111]

So they never come together again, and between them there is established a prohibition like the prohibition of foster-relationship (ḥurmat al-riḍāʿ). This is the view of the three Imams (al-a'immah al-thalathah). The evidences for these opinions, and what supports and what counts against them, are to be sought in the extensive books of jurisprudence (fiqh).

He (al-Alusi's source, or the one being cited) also derived from the legislation of li'an (mutual imprecation) the permissibility of invoking a curse upon a specific liar. His saying ﴿The curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars﴾ is a supplication against himself for a curse on the supposition of his lying. Making it conditional upon that does not take it out of being specific. Yes, it may be said that its legitimacy is conditional upon his being truthful; so if he were lying, it would not be lawful for him.

The Khawarij used as evidence that lying is kufr, because whoever is characterized by it deserves a curse, and likewise that fornication (zina) is kufr, because its doer deserves wrath (ghadab). For each of the curse and the wrath is deserved only by the disbeliever, since la'n (cursing) is expulsion from mercy, which applies only to a disbeliever, and wrath is greater than that.

In response: it is not conceded that la'n, wherever it occurs, means expulsion from mercy, for it may mean removal from the rank of the righteous (al-abrar), and it may be intended to show the baseness of the one cursed. Likewise, it is not conceded that wrath is specific to the disbeliever, even if it is greater than cursing. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 24, verse 10:

﴿Had it not been for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise.﴾ This is a shift (iltifat) to addressing the accusers and the accused, through the device of taghlib (the predominance of one grammatical form over another), so as to give the context of favour its due. The answer to "law la" (had it not been for) is omitted, to magnify it, so that it is as if no expression could encompass its explanation. This omission is common in their speech.

Jarir said:

"The blamers lied, had they seen our camp at Hazeez Ramma while the camels were grazing."

And among their proverbs: "Had it been a woman with bracelets who slapped me..."

So it is as if it were said: "Had it not been for His favour upon you and His mercy, glory be to Him, and that He is exceedingly accepting of repentance, All-Wise in all His acts and rulings, of which is what He legislated for you concerning the rule of li'an (mutual oath-taking between spouses), it would have been something no range of explanation could encompass." Among its aspects is that, had He not legislated that for them, the husband would have been obliged to bear the penalty for slander (hadd al-qadhf), although the apparent truth is his, because he knows his wife's condition best, and he would not fabricate against her since both share the disgrace. And after He legislated it for them, had He made his testimonies a cause for the penalty of adultery (hadd al-zina) upon her, the opportunity to look into her case would have been lost; and had He made his testimonies a cause for the penalty of slander upon him, the opportunity to look into his case would have been lost. There is no doubt that all of this would have departed from the paths of wisdom, grace and mercy. Thus He made the testimony of each of them, while one of them is certainly lying, a decisive means of averting the worldly harm that was directed at them. The liar among them is afflicted, within the repetitions of his testimonies, with a punishment more complete than what it averted from him and more severe. In this are profound wisdoms and effects of grace and mercy that are not hidden. As for the truthful, it is evident. As for the liar, it is His granting him respite, covering him in this world, averting the penalty from him, and exposing him to repentance, as is indicated by the mention of the title "Oft-Returning" (Tawwab) for Him, glory be to Him. So exalted is His majesty, vast is His mercy, and subtle is His wisdom.

Shaykh al-Islam (Abu al-Su'ud) said. And from Ibn Salam, (he interpreted) the favour as Islam. It is not hidden that this is something the context does not require. And from Abu Muslim, that he included in "the favour" the prohibition of adultery. This would be fitting if the sentence were taken as a concluding summary (tadhyil) of all the preceding verses, though there is in it what there is of remoteness.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 24, verse 11 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander (al-ifk)﴾ means: with the most eloquent form of lying and fabrication. It is often explained simply as "lying" in general. It was also said that it is "calumny (buhtan), which comes upon you without your noticing until it suddenly strikes you." It is permissible to read the hamza and the fa' with a fatha (af-ka). Its root is from al-afk, with a fatha followed by a sukun, which means "turning" and "diverting," because a lie is diverted from the course that is right. The intended meaning is what the Truthful One (al-Siddiqah), the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, was accused of, with the definite article being for specific reference (al-'ahd). It is also permissible to take it as generic (al-jins). It was said that in this case it implies restriction (al-qasr), as if to say: there is no slander except that slander. The word "came" (ji'a) indicates that they fabricated it from their own selves, without it having any basis.

The detailed account of the story is what al-Bukhari and others narrated from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said:

"When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended to go out, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever of them the lot came out for, the Messenger of Allah would take her with him." 'A'ishah said: "He drew lots among us in a battle he fought, and my lot came out, so I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after the hijab had been revealed. I was carried in my howdah and I would dismount in it. We travelled until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished that (campaign) and returned, and we approached Madinah on the return journey. He announced the departure one night, so I walked until I passed the army. When I had finished my need, I came back to my riding-place, and suddenly my necklace of Zafar onyx had broken. I searched for my necklace, and its searching detained me. Meanwhile, the men who used to load my riding-beast came and lifted my howdah and placed it on my camel, which I had mounted, and they thought I was in it. Women in those days were light and not weighed down by flesh; they only ate a small morsel of food. So the people did not notice the lightness of the howdah when they lifted it. I was a young girl of tender age, so they sent the camel off and marched. I found my necklace after the army had moved on, so I came to their camping place and there was no one there, neither caller nor answerer. So I went to the place where I had been, thinking that they would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my place, sleep overcame me and I slept. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had been behind the army. He travelled by night and reached my place in the morning. He saw the dark shape of a sleeping person, came to me, and recognised me, for he had seen me before the hijab. I awoke at his saying 'Inna lillah' when he recognised me. I covered my face with my outer garment. By Allah, he did not speak a word to me, nor did I hear from him any word except his saying 'Inna lillah,' when he made his mount kneel and it stepped on its forelegs, and I mounted it. He set off leading the mount with me until we reached the army after they had halted at the height of midday, while they were resting. Then whoever was destroyed because of me was destroyed. The one who took the lead in the slander was 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. We came to Madinah, and I fell ill when I arrived, for a month, while the people were spreading the talk of the slanderers, and I did not perceive anything of that. What troubled me in my illness was that I did not recognise from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the gentleness that I used to see from him when I was ill. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would only come in to me, greet me, and then say: 'How are you?' Then he would leave. That was what troubled me, and I did not perceive the evil. Then I went out after I had recovered, together with Umm Mistah, toward al-Manasi', which was our place for relieving ourselves. We would go out only at night, until night, before we took the latrines near our houses; this was the custom of the early Arabs regarding relieving themselves outside, for we found the latrines near our houses to be a nuisance. So I set out with Umm Mistah, who was the daughter of Abu Rahm ibn 'Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn 'Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son was Mistah ibn Uthathah. Umm Mistah and I came back toward my house after we had finished our need. Umm Mistah stumbled over her cloak and said: 'Mistah has perished!' I said to her: 'What a bad thing you have said! Do you curse a man who fought at Badr?' She said: 'O you! Did you not hear what he said?' I said: 'And what did he say?' So she told me of the saying of the people of the slander, and I became more ill upon my illness. When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me and said: 'How are you?' I said: 'Will you permit me to go to my parents?' She said: 'I wanted at that time to ascertain the news from them.' She said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted me, so I came to my parents and said to my mother: "O mother! What are the people talking about?" She said: "O my daughter, take it easy. By Allah, it rarely happens that a woman who is beautiful, beloved by her husband, and has co-wives, does not have many things said about her." I said: "Subhan Allah! Have the people really spoken of this?" She said: So I wept that night until morning, my tears did not dry up, and I did not close my eyes in sleep until the morning, and I was still weeping. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd when the revelation was delayed, to consult them about separating from his family. As for Usamah ibn Zayd, he advised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and the affection he had for them, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing but good.' As for 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah has not constricted you, and there are many women other than her. Ask the slave-girl and she will tell you the truth.' She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Barirah and said: 'O Barirah, have you seen anything that troubles you?' Barirah said: 'No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I have seen nothing in her that I would criticise, other than that she is a young girl who sleeps and neglects her family's dough, so the domestic goat comes and eats it.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and asked to be excused on that day from 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul." She said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, while on the minbar: 'O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man whose harm has reached me regarding my family? By Allah, I know nothing of my family but good, and they mention a man of whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered upon my family except with me.' Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I will excuse you from him. If he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck; and if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, command us and we will do your bidding.'" She said: "Then Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, who was the chief of the Khazraj, stood up, and he had been a righteous man before that, but zealous passion overcame him. He said to Sa'd: 'You have lied! By the life of Allah, you will not kill him, and you are not able to kill him.' Then Usayd ibn Hudayr, who was the cousin of Sa'd, stood up and said to Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah: 'You have lied! By the life of Allah, we will certainly kill him, for you are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of the hypocrites.' So the two factions of the Aws and the Khazraj were stirred up until they were about to fight each other, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing on the minbar. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept calming them until they fell silent, and he fell silent." She said: "I remained that day without my tears drying up, and I did not close my eyes in sleep. My parents were with me, and I wept for two nights and a day, not closing my eyes in sleep and my tears not drying up. They thought that weeping would split my liver. While they were sitting with me and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter, so I allowed her, and she sat weeping with me. While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon us, greeted us, and sat down." She said: "He had not sat with me since what was said about me had been said, and he had remained a month without revelation concerning my matter." She said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the tashahhud when he sat down, then said: 'Amma ba'd. O 'A'ishah, it has reached me that such and such has been said about you. If you are innocent, Allah will clear you; and if you have committed a sin, then seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses his sin and then repents to Allah, Allah accepts his repentance.'" She said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his speech, my tears dried up until I could not feel a single drop. I said to my father: 'Answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding what he said.' He said: 'By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.' I said to my mother: 'Answer the Messenger of Allah.' She said: 'I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'" She said: "So I said, and I was a young girl who did not recite much of the Qur'an: 'Indeed, by Allah, I know that you have heard this story until it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. So if I say to you that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess to you something, and Allah knows that I am innocent of it, you will believe me. By Allah, I find for myself and for you no example except the saying of the father of Joseph: ﴿So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ [Yusuf: 18].'" Then she lay down on her bed, and at that time she knew that she was innocent and that Allah would clear her by her innocence. But she did not think that Allah would send down a revelation in her matter that would be recited, and her affair in her own estimation was too insignificant for Allah to speak about her in a matter to be recited. Rather, she hoped that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see a dream in which Allah would clear her. She said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not moved from his place, nor had anyone of the household left, until revelation came down upon him. He was seized by the distress that used to seize him, until the sweat would pour from him like pearls, even though it was a winter day, because of the weight of the word that was being revealed to him." She said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was relieved of that, he was relieved and was smiling, and the first word he spoke was: 'O 'A'ishah, Allah has cleared you.' My mother said: 'Get up and go to him.' I said: 'By Allah, I will not get up, and I will praise none but Allah.' And Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander﴾, all ten verses."

And the apparent reading of His saying, exalted is He:
﴿a group among you﴾ is the predicate of "inna" (indeed). This is the view of al-Hawfi and Abu al-Baqa'. Ibn 'Atiyyah said it is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "ja'u" (they came), and the predicate is the clause of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not think it bad for you﴾. The implied meaning is: if those who did it [did so]. He said: this is more coherent in meaning and more beneficial than that ﴿a group﴾ should be the predicate, end of quote. It is not hidden that this is forced. The benefit of the statement in the first view has been said to be consolation, that those who brought that slander were a zealous and mutually supporting faction, and this is one of the signs of its being a slander with no basis. It was also said: the better view is that the consolation lies in that this matter was not agreed upon by all, but was brought by a small handful of you. Abu al-Baqa' claimed that the description of the group as "from you" conveys information, but this is open to question.

The address in ﴿from you﴾, according to what I incline to, is to those among the believers who were distressed by that, and it includes the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umm Ruman, 'A'ishah, and Safwan, by primary inclusion. The root of "'usbah" is a faction bound together by partisanship, whether it is few or many. Its usage became common for ten and above, up to forty, and this is what al-Jawhari restricted himself to in the Sihah. It is also used for fewer than that; in the codex of Hafsah there is "'usbah" of four. It is authentically related that 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, counted among the hypocrites 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Hamnah bint Jahsh, the sister of the Mother of the Believers Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hassan ibn Thabit. Some people exonerated Hassan, but this contradicts what is in the Sahih of al-Bukhari and others.

Indeed, the apparent meaning is that he (Hassan), may Allah be pleased with him, did not say it from the core of his heart, but only transmitted it from Ibn Ubayy, may Allah curse him. It has been reported that he, may Allah be pleased with him, apologised for what was attributed to him regarding 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and said:

A chaste, dignified woman, who never was suspected of doubt, and who wakes up hungry from the flesh of the unwary.
The beloved of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance, possessor of noble qualities and abundant bounties.
The noble lady of a tribe from Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, whose noble endeavours and glory are not diminished.
Refined, whose tent Allah has perfumed and purified from every evil and falsehood.
If you have said what you claim, then may my fingers never raise my whip against me.
And how could they, when my affection and support as long as I live are for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings.
He has ranks high above all people, which the strivings of the arrogant fall short of.
For what has been said is not an illegitimate child, but the saying of a man whose rope has been loosened by me.

Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, would honor him (Hassan) after that and mention him with good. And even if it is authentically reported that she said to him, when he recited to her the first of these verses, "But you are not like that," Ibn Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Sirin that Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, would grant Hassan permission to enter, would have a cushion placed for him, and would say: "Do not harm Hassan, for he used to defend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his tongue."

Ibn Jarir narrated through al-Sha'bi from her that she said: "I have not heard anything better than the poetry of Hassan, and whenever I recited it I hoped Paradise for him," meaning his saying to Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib:

"You satirized Muhammad, and I responded on his behalf,
and with Allah is the recompense for that.
For my father, my mother, and my honor
are a shield against your attack on the honor of Muhammad.
Do you revile him, when you are no match for him?
So your evil is a ransom for your good.
My tongue is a sharp sword with no fault in it,
and my sea is not muddied by buckets."

Some counted Zayd ibn Rifa'a together with the four mentioned, but we have not seen a sound report for this, and it is said to be an error. The meaning of "minkum" (from among you) is: from among the people of your religion and those who belong to Islam, whether that is so in reality or not. Thus it includes Ibn Ubayy, for he is one who belongs to Islam outwardly, even though he was a disbeliever in reality. It is also said that Allah's words ﴿from among you﴾ are in the form of the most common case, and most of that group were sincere believers. Likewise the address in ﴿do not consider it bad for you﴾. It is also said that the address in the first (verse) is to the Muslims, and in this (verse) it is to the chief of those addressed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and to Abu Bakr, Aisha, and Safwan, may Allah be pleased with them, and the speech is directed toward consoling them.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that the address in the second (verse) is to Aisha and Safwan. Further from the truth is the one who claims that it is addressed to those who brought the slander, and who strained to make the "goodness" (of the matter) fit, and perhaps the attribution of this to al-Hasan is not sound. The apparent reading is that the pronoun of the absent party in ﴿do not consider it﴾ refers to the slander.

It is also permitted that it refers to the accusation, or to the verbal noun understood from ﴿they came﴾, or to the grief that befell the Muslims. All of these, as you see, are (possible). And according to what Ibn Atiyya held, it refers to the omitted noun that is added to the noun of "inna", which is in reality the subject. They were forbidden to consider that evil for them, to relieve their minds by removing what would cause their minds to remain troubled. Allah, glorified is He, followed this prohibition with a shift in the statement, saying, ﴿Rather, it is good for you﴾, showing concern for the matter of consolation. The meaning of "rather, it is good for you" is that it is a great good for you, because by patiently bearing it you gain great reward, and your nobility before Allah, may He be exalted, becomes manifest through the sending down of what exalts your status and intensifies the threat against the one who spoke what grieved you. The verses revealed concerning that, according to what you have just heard from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, are ten.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: "Eighteen consecutive verses were revealed, denying the one who slandered Aisha and affirming her innocence." Al-Tabarani narrated from al-Hakam ibn Utayba that he said: "Allah, glorified is He, sent down in it fifteen verses from Surat al-Nur, then he recited until he reached ﴿The impure women are for impure men﴾ [al-Nur: 26]." It seems the disagreement is based on the disagreement about the verse divisions (ru'us al-ayy), and in the Kitab al-Adad of al-Dani (a work on the counting of verses) there is something that agrees with what is related from Ibn Jubayr.

﴿For every man of them﴾, that is, of those who brought the slander, ﴿is what he has earned of sin﴾, that is, the recompense for what he has earned, and this is in proportion to how much he engaged in it, for some of them spoke, some laughed in admiration and approval of what they heard, and some were more involved and some less.

﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part thereof﴾, with a kasra on the kaf (kibrahu). Al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, Abu Raja', Mujahid, al-A'mash, Abu al-Barhasam, Humayd, Ibn Abi Abla, Sufyan al-Thawri, Yazid ibn Qatib, Ya'qub, al-Zaf'arani, Ibn Muqsim, Amra bint Abd al-Rahman, and Surra (recited it) from al-Kisa'i, and Mahbub from Abu Amr (recited it as) "kubarahu" with a damma on the kaf. Both (forms) are verbal nouns of "kibar al-shay'" (the greatness of a thing), and their meaning is one. It is said that "kibr" with a damma means "the greater part," and with a kasra means "initiating the thing." It is also said that it means "sin." The majority hold the first meaning, that is, the one who bears the greater part of it ﴿among them﴾, that is, among those who brought it, ﴿for him is a great punishment﴾ in this world and the Hereafter, or in the Hereafter alone. In the expression with the relative pronoun, the repetition of the predication, the indefinite form of "punishment," and describing it as great, there is an intensification of the gravity of the matter that is not hidden.

The one who "took upon himself the greater part" is, as in Sahih al-Bukhari (a collection of hadith) from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, upon him be the curse of Allah. He used to gather people around him and recount to them the slander, and he was the first to fabricate it and spread it, out of his extreme enmity to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His punishment in the Hereafter, after he is placed in the lowest level of Hellfire, no one can measure its extent except Allah, mighty and majestic. As for in this world, he was branded with the brand of humiliation and his hypocrisy was exposed before the assembled witnesses. He was flogged with two hadd punishments, according to what al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "after the verses were revealed, he (ﷺ) went out to the mosque and summoned Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, and he gathered the people, then recited to them what Allah had sent down of the innocence of Aisha. He sent for Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, and he was brought, and upon him be peace, he had him flogged two hadd punishments. He sent for Hassan, Mistah, and Hamna, and they were struck a painful blow and struck on their necks." It is also said that he (ﷺ) imposed one hadd punishment. Al-Tabarani narrated from Ibn Abbas that he interpreted the punishment in this world as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lashing him eighty lashes, and his punishment in the Hereafter as his destination being the Fire.

It is also said that he was not flogged at all, because he neither confessed nor committed himself to producing evidence against him, so his retribution was delayed until the Day of Resurrection, just as he did not commit himself to producing evidence of his hypocrisy and the occurrence of what would require his killing for that. But this requires consideration.

Some claimed that Mistah was not flogged, and others that he did not flog any of those who brought the slander, since there was no confession and no commitment to producing evidence. In al-Bahr (al-Bahr al-Muhit, a Qur'anic commentary) it is stated that the well-known view is that Hassan, Mistah, and Hamna were flogged. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with a sound chain from Abu Hurayra. This is also found in verses which Ibn Hisham mentioned in the abridgment of the Sira of Ibn Ishaq:

"Hassan has tasted what his people had,
and Hamna, when they said the shameful thing, and Mistah.
They took up the stoning of the unseen, the command of their Prophet,
and the wrath of the Lord of the Mighty Throne, so they were uprooted.
They harmed the Messenger of Allah in it, so they covered
the disgraces of transgression, which He will erase and expose.
And He poured upon them destructive (stones) as if they were
downpours of rain falling from the peaks of the clouds."

It is also said that the one who took upon himself the greater part was Hassan, and they cited what is in Sahih al-Bukhari as well, from Masruq, who said: "Hassan entered upon Aisha and composed verses in praise of her, and said: 'The chaste one of the house.' She said: 'But you are not like that.' I said: 'Do you claim that such a man enters upon you, when Allah has sent down: ﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part thereof among them, for him is a great punishment﴾?' She said: 'And what punishment is greater than blindness?'" It was also reported in some reports that it was said to her: "Does not Allah say: ﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part thereof﴾, the verse?" She said: "Did it not befall him, a great punishment? Has he not lost his sight, and been struck with the sword?" She meant the blow that Safwan struck him with when he learned that he was speaking about that. It is narrated that he struck him with the sword on his head for that reason. The verses in which he (Hassan) alluded to him and to those of the Arabs of Mudar who had embraced Islam, and he recited:

"Keep away from the edge of my sword, for indeed I
am a young man, if I am provoked, you are not a poet.
But I protect what is mine and guard against
the confused of mind, the innocent of appearance."

And he nearly killed him with that blow.

Ibn Ishaq narrated that when he struck him, Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas leapt upon him, bound his hands to his neck with a rope, and took him to the house of the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj. Abd Allah ibn Rawaha met him and said: "What is this?" He said: "Did you not like Hassan being struck with the sword? By Allah, I think he has killed him." Abd Allah said to him: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) know about this and what you have done?" He said: "No, by Allah." He said: "You have been bold. Release the man." So he released him. They came to the Messenger of Allah, upon him be peace, and told him about it. He summoned Hassan and Safwan. Safwan said: "O Messenger of Allah, he harmed me and satirized me, and anger overcame me, so I struck him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Hassan, has the matter of my people become shameful after Allah has guided them to Islam?" Then he said: "Be gracious, O Hassan, regarding what befell you." He said: "It is yours, O Messenger of Allah." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) compensated him for it with Bayruha, which Abu Talha ibn Sahl had given to him, upon him be peace, and he also gave him Sirin, a Coptic slave girl, who bore him Abd al-Rahman ibn Hassan.

In another report in Sahih al-Bukhari, also from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, she said regarding ﴿he who took upon himself the greater part thereof among them﴾: it refers to the hypocrite, Ibn Ubayy, and Hamna. It is also said that it refers to him, Hassan, and Mistah. The punishment of the hypocrite is expulsion and the manifestation of his hypocrisy, and the punishment of the latter two is the loss of sight. The use of the singular relative pronoun does not preclude the intention of a plural, since the relative pronoun "alladhi" (who) may be a plural in meaning, and the singular pronoun referring to it is permissible on the basis of intending the group, the crowd, or the party, or because its form is that of the singular. Its singular form appears in the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And he who came with the truth and believed in it﴾ [al-Zumar: 33], and its plural in His words, glorified is He: ﴿And you plunged as those who plunged﴾ [al-Tawba: 69]. The well-known view is that "alladhi" may be used in the plural without restriction. Ibn Malik stipulated in al-Tashil (a grammatical work) that it must be intended as a class and not a specific plural group, and if a specific group is intended, its use is limited to poetic necessity. However, it is not hidden that the intention of the plural here is not free from remoteness. What he preferred is that the intention is the singular, and that this singular is the enemy of Allah, His Messenger (ﷺ), and the believers, Ibn Ubayy. Al-Zuhri narrated this from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, Alqama ibn Abi Waqqas, and Abd Allah ibn Utba, and all of them heard Aisha say: "The one who took upon himself the greater part" is Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. Many reports have converged on this, and those among the exegetes who hold this view are more numerous than those who hold otherwise.

[Page 116]

Among the fabrications that arose from enmity is the statement of Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, upon him be what Allah, may He be exalted, deserves, when al-Zuhri was asked about "he who took upon himself the greater part": he said to him: "It is Ibn Ubayy." He replied: "You lie, it is Ali." He meant by this the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honor his face. This was narrated from Hisham by al-Bukhari, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. There is no wonder in the Umayyad's fabrication against the Commander of the Faithful Ali, may Allah honor his face and be pleased with him.

You know that the most that was narrated from the Commander, may Allah be pleased with him, is that he said to his brother and cousin, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he consulted him: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has not constricted you, and women other than her are many; and if you ask the slave girl, she will confirm you." In another report he said: "O Messenger of Allah, the people have spoken, and divorcing her has become lawful for you." And in another report, "he, may Allah be pleased with him, struck Barira and said: 'Speak the truth to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).'" There is nothing in any of that that could serve as a basis for that Umayyad, the nasibi (enemy of Ali). The main aim of the Commander in what he mentioned was to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from what he was suffering of grief. The most that can be said is that he did not follow the course of Usama, which is not a binding matter. Whoever examines carefully will recognize the intent of the Commander, may Allah honor his face, and that it is far from what the nawasib claim, as far as the east is from the west. So let him reflect.

Why did you not, when you heard it, say: ﴿It is not for us to speak of this﴾? This is a turn from addressing those who indulged in the slander, excluding those among them who took upon themselves its greater part. Abu Hayyan preferred that the address is to the believers alone, excluding them. The address was chosen to intensify the rebuke contained in *lawla* (why not, an exhortative particle, *lawla al-tahdidiyya*). To strengthen the rebuke, he shifted to the third person in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the believing men and the believing women thought well of their own kind﴾. This is not a manner of turning away from those addressed and reporting their offences to others, but rather a means of describing them with what necessitates doing what they were urged to do. It fully demands it and strongly restrains them from its opposite, which is disbelief in it. Being something that moves them to think well and restrains them from ill thoughts about *their own kind*, that is, members of their own species and people of their own religion, who are placed in the position of their own selves, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not defame one another﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11], and His saying, glorified is He: ﴿then you are those who kill your own selves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 85] [p. 118]. There is no need to posit an elided noun, meaning "the thinking of some of the believing men and women about the selves of others among them." Even if it is said that this is permissible, it is beyond doubt, but their failure to act on what this description requires is more abominable and more shameful. The rebuke for it was included, together with what it contains of a means to rebuke the slandering women, the best known of whom was Hamnah. Then, if by "faith" is meant true faith, its requirement for what was mentioned is clear, and the rebuke is specific to those who possess it. If by it is meant faith in its general sense, which includes what the hypocrites also displayed, then its requirement for them is because they used to guard against displaying anything that contradicted their claim. The rebuke is then directed at all. The point in placing the object of the exhorted verb between it and the particle of restriction, although that is permissible in general (that is, whether the intervening object is an adverbial or otherwise), is to restrict the exhortation to the very first moment of hearing and to confine the rebuke and blame to delaying the performance of what was urged until that moment, with hesitation about it. This serves to show that not performing it at all is of the utmost ugliness and shamefulness. That is, it was obligatory upon the believing men and women that, the first time they heard that lie from the one who invented it, whether directly or through an intermediary, they should think well, without stammering or hesitation, of a member of their own community among the believing men and women. ﴿And say﴾ at that moment: ﴿this is a manifest lie﴾, that is, evident and plain that it is a lie. How then could it be said of the Mother of the Believers, the beloved wife of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the daughter of the emigrants? May Allah be pleased with both of them.

It is also possible that the meaning is: "Why did the believing men and the believing women, the first time they heard that, not think well of their own people, ʿAisha and Safwan, and say..." and so on.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 24, verse 13:

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ This may be part of the speech being urged, coming to rebuke the listeners for failing to hold the slanderers to account. That is, "Why did the slanderers not bring four witnesses who would testify to the truth of what they said?" ﴿Then, since they did not bring the witnesses﴾, the four, and the apparent wording would have been "Then, since they did not bring them," but it was turned to the sublime phrasing for the sake of greater emphasis. ﴿Then those﴾ is a reference to the slanderers, and the distance implied in the demonstrative is to indicate how far their rank has sunk in corruption; that is, "Then those corrupters" ﴿in the sight of God﴾, that is, in His judgments and His law, ﴿they are the liars﴾, that is, those judged to be liars by the Law, meaning that their report did not conform to the actual reality in terms of the Law. It has also been said that the meaning is: "Then those, in the knowledge of God Most High, are the liars whose report did not conform to the reality as it is in itself, because the verse concerns specifically 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, and the report of the People of the Slander concerning her was not in accordance with the reality as it is in itself, in the knowledge of Him, Mighty and Majestic."

It has been objected that the specificity of the occasion of revelation does not negate the generality of the ruling, and that the apparent restriction by the adverbial phrase rejects this. He also considered it comparable to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Now God has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you﴾ [al-Anfal: 66], which is contrary to the apparent meaning. Whatever the case, the restriction serves emphasis. Alternatively, it is a independent statement issued from Him, glory be to Him and exalted, confirming that this was a fabrication.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 24, verse 14:

﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah﴾ — that is, His bounty, glorified is He — ﴿upon you, and His mercy﴾ toward you ﴿in this world﴾ through the various kinds of blessings, among which is the granting of respite for repentance (and in the Hereafter) through the various kinds of favours, among which is pardon and forgiveness after repentance. In the speech there is an unfolding (nashr) in the order of the folding (laff). It is also permitted that ﴿in this world and the Hereafter﴾ be connected to each of "the grace of Allah" and "His mercy," and the meaning is: had it not been for the general grace and the general mercy in both abodes, ﴿you would have been touched﴾ immediately (for what you plunged into) — that is, because of what you immersed yourselves in of the discourse of the slander.

The vagueness is for the sake of magnifying its matter and deeming its mention repugnant. It is said: afada fi al-hadith (he plunged into the talk), khada (he waded), hadhdhaba (he rushed), and indafa'a (he surged), with the same meaning. The "plunging" (ifada) in this is a metaphor drawn from pouring water into a vessel. (And had it not been) is the particle of prevention (imtina'iyyah), and its answer is (﴿a tremendous punishment would have touched you﴾)
Page 119
which makes the rebuke and the lashing seem trivial by comparison. The address is to those other than Ibn Ubayy among the plungers, and it is permitted that it be to all of them.

It has been objected that Ibn Ubayy, the head of the hypocrites, has no share of Allah's mercy in the Hereafter, because he is eternally abiding in the lowest level of the Fire.

﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾. The letter *tā'* has been elided from *tatalaqqawnahu* (one of the two *tā'*s is dropped). *Idh* (when) is an adverbial clause modifying *al-mass* (touched): the great punishment touched you at the time you received it. It is permissible for *idh* to modify *afadtum* (you plunged into), but that is not the correct view. The pronoun in *ma* (the object) refers to what you plunged into: that great punishment touched you at the time you received the falsehood you were immersed in, and at the time some of you took it from others by asking about it. *Talaqqī*, *talaqquf* and *talaqqun* have closely related meanings, but *talaqqī* carries the sense of meeting or facing, *talaqquf* carries the sense of snatching or taking quickly, and *talaqqun* carries the sense of skill and dexterity.

Ubayy (Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him) read *tatalaqqūnahu* in its original form. Al-Bazzi read the *tā'* with a shadda (doubling), and the two grammarians (al-Nahwiyyān, i.e. Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i, as commonly identified) and Hamza assimilated the *dhāl* into the *tā'*.

Ibn al-Sumayfa' read *talquhu* with a *ḍamma* on the *tā'* and *qāf*, and a sukun on the *lām*, as the imperfect of *alqā* (to cast). From him also is *talqawnahu* with a *fatḥa* on the *tā'* and *qāf* and a sukun on the *lām*, as the imperfect of *laqiya* (to meet). ʿĀʾisha, Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), ʿĪsā, Ibn Yaʿmur and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read with a *fatḥa* on the *tā'*, a *kasra* on the *lām* and a *ḍamma* on the *qāf*, from *walaqa al-kalām*, meaning his lying (*kadhibuhu*). This was related by al-Sarqusṭī. In this there is a refutation of those who claimed that *waliqa*, when it means "to lie," is not transitive. This is the apparent meaning of the words of Ibn Sayyidah, and Abū Ḥayyān approved of it; for this reason he considered it to be of the type of elision and conveyance (*al-ḥadhf wal-īṣāl*), the original being *tulqūna fīhi* (you cast into it).

It is related from ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) that she used to read it this way and say: *al-walaq* is lying. Ibn Abī Malīka said:

*She was more knowledgeable about this than others, because it was revealed concerning her.*

Ibn al-Anbārī said: whoever *walaqa al-ḥadīth* (fabricated the speech) invented and originated it. It was also said: whoever *walaqa al-kalām* arranged it. al-Ṭabarī and others related that this word is derived from *al-walaq*, which is hastening with one thing after another, like a number following a number and speech following speech. It is said: *nāqa walqā* (a swift she-camel). From this comes *al-awlaq* for the madman, because reason is a form of stillness and composure, while madness is a form of haste and rashness.

From Ibn Jinnī, he explained what is in the verse by what has been mentioned, so that it is of the type of elision and conveyance, the original being *tusrikūna fīhi aw ilayhi* (you hasten into it or towards it).

Zayd ibn Aslam and Abū Jaʿfar read *ta'lqūnahu* with a *fatḥa* on the *tā'*, a sukun on a following hamza, and a sukun on the following *lām*, from *al-alq*, which is lying. Yaʿqūb, in the transmission of al-Māzinī, read *taylqūnahu* with a *kasra* on the upper *tā'*, followed by a *yā'*, and a *fatḥa* on the *lām*, as if it were the imperfect of *walaqa* with a *kasra* on the *lām*, just as they said *tījal* as the imperfect of *wajila*. From Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna: I heard my mother reading *idh tathqafūnahu* (when you overtake it), from *thaqaftu al-shay'* when you seek it and find it; it comes heavy and light, meaning you hunt down speech about the falsehood from here and from there.

It was also read *taqifūnahu*, from *qafāhu*, when he follows him, meaning you follow it.

﴿And you say with your mouths what is not known to you﴾. That is, you say a saying confined to the mouths, without having any reality or source in the hearts, since it is not an expression of knowledge in your hearts. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 167]. Ibn al-Munīr said: His saying, glorified is He, ﴿and you say with your mouths﴾ may be a rebuke, like your saying: "Do you say that with your full mouth?" For the speaker may hint and allude, or may speak boldly with affected certainty like a knowledgeable person. This has been said regarding His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Hatred has appeared from their mouths﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 118]. The author of *al-Farā'id* said: It is possible to say that the benefit of mentioning *"with your mouths"* is that one should not think they said that with the heart, because *qawl* (saying) is applied to what does not proceed from the mouths, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "We come willingly"﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 11], and the saying of the poet:

*The pool became full and said: "Qaṭnī, gently, gently, you have filled my belly."*

So it is an emphasis to remove metaphor. You know that the context requires the first meaning, and al-Zamakhsharī went to it. The apparent expression would have been *wa-taqūlūnahu bi-afwāhikum*, but it deviated from it to what is in the sublime arrangement, for reasons that are not hidden.

﴿And you consider it trivial﴾, easy, with no consequence for it; ﴿while it is in the sight of Allah great﴾, that is, while the state is that it is with Allah, exalted and majestic is He, a great matter whose measure cannot be estimated in terms of the burden of sin and the drawing down of punishment. The two verbal clauses are conjoined to the clause ﴿you received it﴾ and are within the scope of *idh* along with it. Thus the touching of the great punishment is linked to their receiving the falsehood with their tongues and speaking of it without deliberation or thought, while they reckon that to be something of no concern, and it is, in the sight of Allah, exalted and majestic, great.

**Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 24, verse 16:**

﴿And why, when you heard it,﴾ from the one who invented it or who followed him, ﴿did you not say,﴾ as a denial of it and an expression of horror at what he committed, ﴿It is not for us to speak of this﴾, meaning: it is not possible for us, and it does not befit us in any way, to speak of it. ﴿This﴾ refers to the statement they heard, considered in terms of its particular instance.

It is also permissible that it refers to its category, since slandering individual people who are characterized by chastity (*ihsan*) is forbidden by the Law. There has come from Hudhayfa, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), that it "erases the deeds of a hundred years." This is especially so when it touches the honour of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)'s wife, the *Siddiqa* (the truthful one, i.e., 'A'isha). The discussion concerning the placement of the adverbial phrase here is as has already passed.

﴿Glory be to You﴾ is an expression of amazement at the one who utters it. Its original use is to be said when witnessing something wondrous among the works of God, exalted is His majesty, as a declaration of His transcendence above anything being difficult for Him, such as the like of it. Then it became common until it was used for anything that one marvels at. Its use in the sense mentioned here is a figurative usage (*majaz*) based on metonymy (*kinaya*). Similar to its use to express amazement is "There is no god but Allah." The common people also use the blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in that context, but this is not found in the language of the Law. Indeed, some jurists have explicitly prohibited it.

It is also permissible that ﴿Glory be to You﴾ here is used in its literal sense, and that the intended meaning is to declare God, exalted is His majesty, transcendent above allowing His Prophet, upon him blessings and peace, to be stained and disgraced. The immorality of a wife is a stain upon the husband, from which hearts recoil and souls are kept from following him. For this reason God, exalted is He, protected the wives of the prophets, upon them be peace, from this. This is unlike disbelief, for a wife's disbelief is not a stain upon the husband. It is said that the disbelief of the wives of Noah and Lot, upon them both be peace, is established, and what relates to this will come shortly, God willing.
